item.title: Kaga Yuzen: A Hands-On Silk Dyeing Craft Experience — Guide
item.description: Kaga Yuzen is one of Japan’s most refined silk dyeing traditions, distinguished from Kyoto’s better-known Yuzen style by its more naturalistic, subtly shaded motifs of flowers, birds and autumn leaves rendered in five traditional colours (indigo, crimson, ochre, dark green and violet). The technique developed in Kanazawa under Maeda clan patronage, and visitors can try hands-on workshops today, working under artisan guidance to dye a small piece of silk or a simple item like a handkerchief, offering a genuine introduction to a craft that traditionally takes years to master.

item.title: Kanazawa Crafts: Gold Leaf, Kutani Pottery, Kaga Yuzen & Wajima Lacquer
item.description: Kanazawa’s extraordinary concentration of traditional crafts is not accidental. The Maeda lords who ruled Kaga Domain for three centuries were deliberate patrons of craft culture, importing master artisans from Kyoto and other craft centres to establish and elevate the regional traditions. Unable to spend their wealth on military expansion (the Tokugawa peace made warfare impossible), the Maeda channelled resources into ceramics workshops, silk dyeing studios, and gold leaf production on a scale that made Kanazawa the pre-eminent craft city of Japan outside Kyoto.
